newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai companies asked to set up provident funds.
newsitem.headline: Thai companies asked to set up provident funds.

text.p: The Thai cabinet on Tuesday approved a proposal requiring eligible companies to set up provident funds for employees, cabinet sources said.
The proposed Finance Ministry scheme would cover listed Thai companies, infrastructure operators, and firms enjoying tax concession privileges from the Board of Investment.
The cabinet sources said private companies in the groups would have 18 months to launch provident funds to which employers and employees would each contribute three to 10 percent of staff salaries.
They said the affected companies could seek an initial three-year delay to start the provident funds if they were financially unprepared to launch them.

The sources said employee contributions to the funds would be voluntary and those by employers would be tax-deductible. They said the measure would help mobilise about 4.6 billion baht ($184 million) of domestic savings annually.
